title: Associate, Operations Compliance
description:
IPX Power, a clean energy company, develops, owns, and operates some of the world’s largest energy resources, delivering affordable, reliable power to utilities and other customers. We are in a rapid growth phase with 4.3 GW of solar PV and 8.8 GWh of battery storage in construction or operation, with more projects under various stages of development.

IPX is a profitable, well capitalized, independent power producer that has delivered billions of dollars of industrial-scale clean energy infrastructure. The company was recently formed as a spin-out of Intersect, as a result of their recent acquisition by Google. IPX is supported by long-standing existing investors TPG Rise Climate, Climate Adaptive Infrastructure, and Greenbelt Capital Partners.

IPX is rooted in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and operational excellence. We are building and operating billions of dollars in assets and seeking people eager to develop, build, and operate one of the world’s largest renewables and storage portfolios.

About this Position

The role will support operating utility-scale power generation projects with compliance work, primarily involving NERC processes and regulatory requirements. Its baseline focus is NERC compliance, with exposure to ISOs/RTOs and PUC regulations. The position is intended for an analyst who can develop in the role and contribute to operating assets, including projects such as Easley and Darden. The role is expected to begin with a limited project assignment and expand as the individual gains experience. The person will help identify how activities at operating sites affect regulatory obligations and will contribute to responses to regulator requests for information.

Role and responsibilities

  • Support operating projects with NERC processes and other compliance tasks; help curate responses to regulators' requests for information; stay apprised of site activities; and assess whether activities create regulatory compliance impacts, obligations, or process requirements. The role will also involve understanding the regulatory requirements that apply during project operations and completing compliance work needed before projects move into operations.
  • The role will initially support 2 or 3 sites before widening its scope. Current work is focused on assets in operations, while exposure to project onboarding includes the transition from construction to operations.
  • Will interact with regulators, operating-site personnel, legal or regulatory teams, operations teams, and colleagues involved in cybersecurity and SCADA.

Qualifications and Skills

Required:

  • Experience leading operational readiness and compliance initiatives for operating assets, managing ongoing operational support while successfully transitioning newly constructed projects into active operations.
  • Proficiency in interpreting regulatory requests, navigating site-level operational activities, and translating field work into actionable compliance workflows.
  • Background operating as a generalist across diverse organizational frameworks, managing compliance requirements across cyber, operational, and planning standards.
  • Foundation in regulatory, compliance, or related operating-project work:
  • Willingness to learn across both cyber-related standards and operations-and-planning standards.
  • Experience understanding how operating-site activities can affect regulatory obligations.
  • Experience as a regulatory analyst, compliance analyst, NERC compliance analyst, regulatory associate, or compliance associate
  • Demonstrated experience in project management and cross-functional communication, with exceptional attention to detail.

Nice to have

  • Exposure to ISOs/RTOs, including CAISO or ERCOT
  • Prior work for a consultant or another independent power producer
  • Reported to legal, regulatory, or operations teams
  • Experience moving a project from construction to operations
  • Public Utility Commission regulatory experience
  • Experience with policy and procedure building
  • Experience operating projects or assets in the power-generation industry
  • Knowledge of NERC processes, ISO/RTO environments, and PUC regulations.

Total Rewards

We care about your well-being, growth, and balance. Here’s how we support you:

Compensation: USD $143,750 (displayed total compensation includes base salary + bonus)
Health & Wellness: 100% premium coverage for you and your dependents on medical, dental, and vision
Time to Recharge: Unlimited PTO, plus two company-wide breaks (Fourth of July & end of year)
Family Support: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, plus 6 additional weeks for birth parents; access to family planning support via Maven
Mental Health: Free access to Spring Health which includes 5 free Therapy & psychiatry sessions, plus a Headspace account for mindfulness and meditation through our physical health vendor, Wellhub+
Retirement: 3% non-elective employer contribution to your 401k or RRSP, ensuring your financial future is on the right track
Perks & Extras: $150 monthly food stipend, $150 monthly reimbursement for cell phone/ internet, pet insurance allowance, full home office setup and free access to UrbanSitter with $625 in quarterly paid company credits, Wellhub+, Perkspot, and One Medical

title: Commissioning Project Manager, Construction
description:
IPX Power, a clean energy company, develops, owns, and operates some of the world’s largest energy resources, delivering affordable, reliable power to utilities and other customers. We’re in a rapid growth phase with 4.3 GW of solar PV and 8.8 GWh of battery storage in construction or operation, with more projects under various stages of development. The company was recently formed as a spin-out of Intersect, as a result of their recent acquisition by Google. IPX is supported by long-standing existing investors TPG Rise Climate, Climate Adaptive Infrastructure, and Greenbelt Capital Partners.

IPX is rooted in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and operational excellence. We’re building and operating billions of dollars in assets and seeking people eager to develop, build, and operate one of the world’s largest renewables and storage portfolios.

About This Role
 The Commissioning Project Manager, Construction will oversee and execute the commissioning phase of PV and BESS energy projects. This role manages the transition of utility-scale assets from mechanical completion through initial synchronization and grid integration, to commercial operation and final operation turnover. You will guide the execution of PV performance testing and battery storage capacity and efficiency testing, and ensure projects meet all contractual guarantees and achieve full commercial market participation.

This role interfaces closely with EPC contractors and major equipment OEMs, and manages project schedule and owner-side consultants. Internally, this role requires close coordination with teams across Development, Engineering, Procurement, Origination, Finance, Legal, and Operations. The successful candidate will be comfortable managing multiple large-scale infrastructure projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.


Team Overview
 The Construction team is responsible for the successful execution of IPX Power’s utility-scale renewable energy projects across North America. The team works closely with Development, Engineering, Procurement, Origination, Finance, and Operations to manage EPC contractors, oversee project schedules and budgets, and ensure projects are delivered safely and efficiently. Project Managers coordinate owner-side consultants, contractors, and internal stakeholders to drive projects from construction start through commissioning and operational handover while maintaining high standards for safety, quality, and performance.

What You’ll Do

  • Guide commissioning and grid integration: Manage the commissioning execution of various grid-connected PV and BESS projects through initial synchronization, commercial operations, and substantial completion.
  • Manage performance and capacity testing: Engage with EPC Contractors and OEMs to establish testing procedures and guide testing through to successful achievement of guarantees and full market participation.
  • EPC and OEM Contract Management: Manage contract deliverables, technical submittals, and performance guarantees with EPC partners and OEMs.
  • Interconnection and SCADA Coordination: Coordinate with the Participating Transmission Owner, Grid operator, third party scheduling coordinators, and internal teams to manage test schedules and resource integration processes.
  • Operational Handover: Drive the transition of the physical plant and all technical documentation to the IPX O&M team.
  • Enforce Safety and Compliance: Maintain oversight of site safety, ensuring compliance with site-specific safety plans, safety standards, and local environmental permitting requirements.
  • Internal Project Management: Support cross-functional teams with commissioning reporting and documentation, coordinate with Owner’s Engineers to ensure engineering deliverables meet project specifications, coordinate with Origination team to ensure compliance with Power Purchase Agreements, synchronize with other Project Management team members and mentor associate project managers to support their development, review and manage engineering documentation including RFIs, submittals, transmittals, IFC drawings, and as-built packages, and prepare internal project updates and reports for executive leadership

What You’ll Bring

  • Education (Preferred): Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Experience: 5+ years of commissioning or start-up engineering experience on utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage systems. Experience serving as Project Manager or equivalent role on at least two large-scale infrastructure projects from NTP through substantial completion.
  • Expertise: Direct experience commissioning large-scale PV and BESS projects, including familiarity with power conversion systems, battery management systems, thermal management, and fire suppression systems. Strong understanding of performance testing. Solid understanding of EPC contracts, interconnection agreements, ISO and utility testing requirements, and telemetry/SCADA architectures.
  • Tools and Skills: Advanced proficiency with Excel, Google Workspace, Slack, and Bluebeam. Ability to translate complex project information into clear reports and presentations for executive stakeholders. Strong communication, organization, and stakeholder management skills. High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment. Familiarity with construction safety practices and field coordination.

Health & Wellness: 100% premium coverage for you and your dependents on medical, dental, and vision

title: Senior Electrical Engineer, High Voltage
description:
IPX Power, a clean energy company, develops, owns, and operates some of the world’s largest energy resources, delivering affordable, reliable power to utilities and other customers. We’re in a rapid growth phase with 4.3 GW of solar PV and 8.8 GWh of battery storage in construction or operation, with more projects under various stages of development.
IPX is a profitable, well capitalized, independent power producer that has delivered billions of dollars of industrial-scale clean energy infrastructure. The company was recently formed as a spin-out of Intersect, as a result of their recent acquisition by Google. IPX is supported by long-standing existing investors TPG Rise Climate, Climate Adaptive Infrastructure, and Greenbelt Capital Partners.
IPX is rooted in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and operational excellence. We’re building and operating billions of dollars in assets and seeking people eager to develop, build, and operate one of the world’s largest renewables and storage portfolios

About This Role

The Electrical Engineer will lead the end-to-end technical execution of high-voltage (HV) switchyards, substations, and medium-voltage (MV) systems across utility-scale solar and battery energy storage projects. This role serves as the central hub for critical engineering decisions, ensuring that switchyards are engineered, designed, and constructed strictly up to utility standards for seamless interconnection and handover. Additionally, you will own critical technical engineering decisions spanning utility interconnection of generation facilities, transmission design optimization, and MV collection system performance —from early-stage development through financing, construction, commissioning, and into operations. The role requires a strong balance of technical depth in HV switchyard/substation design and power system studies, combined with elite technical workstream management skills. You will direct EPCs, coordinate with utilities and equipment vendors, and align internal cross-functional teams to drive projects across the finish line on schedule and within budget.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the technical program lifecycle for the design, engineering, and execution of HV substations and switchyards (115kV–500kV), ensuring all designs strictly adhere to interconnecting utility standards and specifications.
  • Act as the primary technical liaison between internal teams, utilities, equipment vendors, and EPCs to manage utility interconnection requirements, design approvals, and switchyard handover processes.
  • Drive clear Divisions of Responsibility (DOR) matrices between the IPP, EPCs, and interconnecting utilities to solidify technical boundaries and delivery schedules.
  • Continuously audit program health to identify engineering or execution gaps and deploy proactive countermeasures to ensure successful switchyard energization and handover.
  • Direct EPCs, Engineers of Record, and consultants to optimize substation and transmission designs, reduce execution risk, and maintain schedule and cost targets.
  • Own the utility interconnection scope, including the technical review of applications, steady-state/dynamic models, and technical negotiations with ISOs and utilities (e.g.,CAISO, ERCOT).
  • Provide NERC and regional regulatory (CAISO/ERCOT) compliance support, ensuring operational readiness and adherence to PRC, MOD, and related standards.
  • Develop and maintain engineering standards, technical specifications, EPC exhibits, and testing protocols.
  • Witness and evaluate FAT/SAT, commissioning, and energization activities.
  • Support EPC RFPs and supply agreements by defining enforceable technical requirements and evaluating vendor proposals.
  • Contribute to Independent Engineer (IE) diligence and technical documentation for project financing.

What You’ll Bring

  • Minimum 12+ years of experience leading technical scope and engineering programs for HV substations (345kV–500kV) and MV collection systems within an IPP, Utility, EPC, or engineering firm.
  • Proven experience managing EPCs, consultants, major equipment vendors, and cross-functional teams through a project's lifecycle.
  • Direct experience with FACTS & Series Compensation, including fixed series capacitors for high-voltage transmission lines, SVCs, STATCOMs, and other Flexible AC Transmission Systems.
  • Strong working knowledge of NERC PRC & MOD standards and regional requirements (CAISO, ERCOT) related to transmission facility and plant operational compliance.
  • Deep understanding of HV/MV equipment, protection and control schemes, metering, substation SCADA, and design trade-offs (technical vs. cost vs. schedule).
  • Solid foundation in power system studies and working knowledge of steady-state modeling tools (ETAP, SKM, DIgSILENT, CDEGS, Aspen, or similar).
  • Advanced Excel skills for technical, performance, and financial analysis.
  • Familiarity with industry codes and standards (NEC, NESC, IEEE).
  • PE (Professional Engineer) license is highly preferred.
  • Bachelors in Electrical Engineering (or related field); Masters or PhD is a plus.
Total Rewards
